subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC — post-call recap and next steps

Hi John — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of your needs:
- Primary requirement: strict data isolation for PII and customer data (no co-mingling with other customers)
- Desired deployment: Private VPC or on-prem if we cannot meet controls via Dedicated capacity
- Key constraints: customer-managed KMS, audit logging / retention policy, and no external model training on customer data

What Redwood can do (high-level):
- Dedicated capacity: physically isolated GPU pools, tenant isolation at runtime, but control plane in Redwood-managed environment (logs + metrics routed to Redwood)
- Private VPC: customer-managed VPC with private control plane and optional on-prem package; supports KMS/HSM integrations and keeps network egress restricted to your environment

Immediate asks / next steps: 
1) Marissa and I will share our security evidence pack (SOC2 summary, network topology) and a short comparison doc that calls out the data flows for Dedicated vs Private VPC.
2) Can you confirm whether FinSecure requires customer-hosted control plane (on-prem) or if a Private VPC with customer KMS and strict egress controls is sufficient?
3) Please share any specific audit log retention windows or compliance requirements we should include in the MOU.

Deliverables we’ll send today: SOC2 summary, simplified topology image, and a draft MOU for review.

If you’re available next week, we can set a 30-min security deep dive with our infra/security lead (Marissa) to run through technical controls.

Thanks — Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
[attachment: SOC2-Summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: John Doe <john.doe@finsecure.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal@finsecure.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Primary preference is Private VPC with customer-managed KMS (we need to control keys). On-prem is an option but adds procurement and longer timelines.
- Audit logging: retention of 7 years for transaction logs and 1 year for debug-level traces (SOC will confirm exact buckets).
- No data from FinSecure may be used for model training or telemetry outside our VPC.

Two quick Qs: 
1) For Private VPC, does Redwood run any control-plane processes that would see raw request payloads? If so, can those be disabled or restricted to metadata only?
2) If we start with Dedicated capacity, can we opt into key-management and encryption controls to approximate isolation until Private VPC is ready?

Happy to do the security deep dive next Tue or Wed morning (PST).

—John
John Doe
Security Architect, FinSecure
john.doe@finsecure.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@finsecure.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC — post-call recap and next steps

Hi John — thanks for the clarifications. Short answers up front, followed by details attached.

1) Control plane visibility: In Private VPC deployments, the control plane can be configured so that request payloads do not leave your VPC. By default our hosted control plane stores minimal metadata for routing/health; for Private deployments we support a private control plane option that keeps payloads customer-side and supports customer-hosted connectors. We can provide an architecture diagram showing which processes run in-customer vs Redwood-managed.

2) Dedicated capacity interim: yes — Dedicated offers strong runtime isolation (dedicated GPU pools) and we can enable customer-managed encryption at rest for model KV caches and persistent storage slices. However, Dedicated will still have a Redwood-managed control plane unless you move to Private. That means things like rollout orchestration and some metrics live with Redwood. For teams that require zero-control-plane visibility, Private (VPC or on-prem) is the supported path.

Attachments included: SOC2-Summary.pdf, redwood-private-vpc-topology.png, draft-mou-finsecure.docx

Proposed next steps: 
- Security deep dive: Tue Apr 6, 10:00–10:30 PST (Marissa, Mateo, Rachel + your security + legal). Can you confirm?
- If you confirm Private VPC is preferred, Marissa will prep a bill-of-materials (network, infra, timeline) and we’ll include an initial statement of controls in the MOU.

Quick note on training telemetry: we can contractually guarantee no customer data is used for model training outside your environment and add that clause to the MOU.

Cheers — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
